title: How would you estimate how many ride-hailing trips are taken in London each day?
description: A step-by-step estimate for "How many ride-hailing trips are taken in London each day?" with the approach, the maths and a sanity check.
hook: Daily trips depend on a small share of people, so the share you choose drives the whole answer. Defend it carefully. Have a go at your own estimate before reading on.
body:
The question

How many ride-hailing trips are taken in London each day?

The approach

People × share taking a trip today × trips each.

Tip: Name the assumption that matters most, so the interviewer knows where the estimate is most sensitive.

Step by step

  1. People in London: 9M
  2. × 3% take a ride-hailing trip on a given day
  3. × 1.5 trips each (often there and back)

That gives about 405k trips a day.

Does it make sense?

Visitors and commuters from outside London would add to this.

Check demand using drivers and completed journeys

The original demand-side estimate gives 405,000 daily trips. For a cross-check, suppose 50,000 active drivers complete eight rides each per day on average. That gives 400,000 trips, but the inputs are hypothetical and the estimate is highly sensitive to part-time drivers and the time spent waiting between trips.

An average day masks a peak problem: airport arrivals, Friday nights, bad weather and transport disruptions all increase demand at particular times. In a platform case, compare completed trips with requested trips and cancellations, and measure the share of time drivers are engaged.

Also clarify whether the client needs ride-hailing journeys within the London boundary, journeys taken by London residents or rides begun at London airports. Those populations overlap but are not identical. The boundaries matter if you later size the platform's accessible market.
